title: Role ownership audit and evidence automation notes
content:
Purpose

Working notes for: aligning RBAC v2 role ownership data, producing evidence for quarterly access reviews, and automating the SIEM export + evidence bundle so that Audit / Compliance can sign off with minimal manual effort. This is an engineering-forward runbook + list of open questions for the quarter.

Scope / assumptions
- Applies to roles labelled in the RBAC v2 catalog (roles stored in auth-service with canonical ids).
- Privileged roles = any role that grants admin-level write/delete over prod clusters, secrets, key management, or service account impersonation.
- Evidence must provide a snapshot of: role membership, last sign-in/access, justifications (owner comments), and an audit-log-backed activity sample for the review period.

High-level deliverables
1) Role ownership inventory extract (CSV) keyed by role_id, role_name, owner(s), created_at, last_modified_at, environment_scope.
2) Evidence bundle per role: 
   - membership.csv (user/service-account, membership_type, added_at, source-ticket)
   - activity-sample.jsonl (filtered audit events for the review window)
   - owner-justification.txt (freeform rationale / renewal intent)
3) SIEM mappings documentation (fields, types, retention, tag mappings) for SOC ingest.
4) Automation pipeline: nightly RBAC export -> transform -> S3 -> Airflow DAG to call SIEM ingestion API + archive bundle for compliance.

Role inventory: quick snapshot (fields we need)
- role_id: uuid
- role_name: human-friendly
- role_type: system|team|service
- owner: username/email (primary)
- owner_secondary: list
- scope: prod|staging|dev|global
- privileged_flag: true|false
- created_at, last_modified
- last_accessed_sample: iso8601 (from audit index)

Audit log schema mapping (current auth-service -> SIEM field suggestions)
Notes: we want every audit event that influences role membership or grants elevated rights. Also capture token creation/impersonation and key usage.

- source_service -> event.source
- event_type -> event.action (e.g. membership.add, membership.remove, role.update, token.create, key.encrypt)
- actor -> user.email (or service_account)
- target_role -> resource.role_id
- target_resource -> resource.id (e.g., project/gke-cluster/secret)
- timestamp -> event.timestamp
- request_id -> event.request_id (traceability)
- ip_address -> network.ip
- change_summary -> event.diff (where available)
- trace_id -> event.trace_id (for cross-service hop correlation)

Suggested SIEM index fields (Elasticsearch/Kibana or Splunk naming)
- @timestamp, source, event.action, actor.email, actor.type, resource.id, resource.type, role_id, role_name, request_id, trace_id, src_ip, outcome

Sample KQL / ES query to pull membership-related events for role "infra-admin" for the quarter:
- index: audit-*
- query (KQL): "event.action : (\"membership.add\" or \"membership.remove\" or \"role.update\") and resource.role_name : \"infra-admin\" and @timestamp >= \"2026-01-01\" and @timestamp <= \"2026-03-31\""

Data transformation rules (during export)
- Normalize actor identifier to email/service-account format. If service account, prefix with sa: for clarity.
- Expand group memberships: if membership source=group (SCIM/G Suite), attach resolved user list snapshot (to avoid future divergence).
- Redact PII fields not required (phone, home address) before archiving bundles for compliance reviewers.
- Enrich events with role tags (privileged_flag, env) from role inventory at export time.

Automation pipeline sketch
1) nightly-export-rbac (auth-service endpoint /admin/export-roles?since=last) -> S3://redwood-audit/exports/rbac/yyyy-mm-dd/role-inventory.csv
2) transform-rbac (lambda/container) -> produce per-role bundle including membership.csv and owner-justification.txt; store under same date prefix
3) collect-audit-sample (ES query job) -> write activity-sample.jsonl for each privileged role (limit sample to 100 events or 1MB)
4) package-bundles -> create tar.gz and compute sha256; write a manifest.json (with flat fields only)
5) siem-ingest-dag (Airflow) -> call SIEM API to upload manifest + metadata + sample events; copy archive to long-term GCS for evidence retention

Operational details / retention
- Evidence retention policy for quarterly recert: archive bundles for 7 years (audit requirement). Keep daily raw exports for 90 days, then only archived monthly tarballs.
- SIEM index retention: hot index 30d, warm 180d, cold/archival for 3 years (per legal).

Acceptance criteria for a role recert
- role has at least one owner listed and owner responded to last recert notice OR owner auto-escalated to manager/contact-list within 14 days.
- membership list has been snapshot and attached.
- activity-sample demonstrates either: no privileged actions OR documented business need for continued access.
- manifest checksum present and uploaded to compliance S3 bucket.

Owner & responsibilities (proposal)
- Role inventory export: eng-auth (Priya Raman)
- SIEM mapping + ingestion: sec-ops (Liam O'Connor)
- Evidence packaging, archive + DAG: infra-automation (Ethan Wu)
- Compliance sign-off/workflow: security-and-compliance (Maya Chen)

Open questions / decisions to make
1) Scope of privileged: include service accounts that can impersonate other users? (my recommendation: yes; treat impersonation as privileged).
2) Sampling policy: how to choose the activity-sample? last N events OR stratified across event-types and actor types? (we should do stratified sampling: ensure at least one admin write and one token create if they exist).
3) Who gets auto-escalation when owner is unresponsive? Manager -> GSuite group owner? Need org chart linkage.
4) Should the owner-justification be templated (checkboxes + freeform) to standardize evidence? I think yes.

Action items (short-term)
- [ ] Priya: add an export endpoint to include resolved group members by 2026-03-05. (JIRA: JIRA-AUD-4123)
- [ ] Liam: draft SIEM field mapping document and share with SOC by 2026-03-07.
- [ ] Ethan: prototype Airflow DAG that pulls one day's exports and packages bundles; push branch to github by 2026-03-10.
- [ ] Maya: draft owner justification template and pilot on infra-admin role by 2026-03-12.

Notes from sync 2026-02-26
- SOC wants both role_id and role_name in every event: role_id for canonical joins, role_name for easy reviewer reading.
- Compliance will accept a 100-event sample for large roles but prefers representative sampling.
- We confirmed we will not include full membership diffs older than 90 days in the fast bundle — those remain in long-term archive.

Appendix: example manifest.json (flat fields only, no nested structures)
- manifest_id: md5 of tar.gz
- bundle_date: 2026-03-01
- role_id: abc123-def4-...
- role_name: infra-admin
- owner: priya@redwood.ai
- sample_count: 87
- archive_path: s3://redwood-audit/archive/2026-03-01/infra-admin-bundle.tar.gz
- sha256: <hex>
- redaction_level: minimal

Unresolved implementation notes (internal)
- Need to validate timezones when slicing audit events (use UTC everywhere).
- Ensure request_id propagation across services: add a check in runtime-telemetry pipeline to surface missing IDs.
- Confirm legal's minimum retention period for access recert evidence (I've asked Legal; waiting response).

If you are reading this and want to volunteer to help implement the DAG or approve the SIEM mapping, ping me (Maya) on #sec-compliance or add a comment on JIRA-AUD-4123.

-- end of notes (working draft)
